articleTitle: An Analog Interface Circuit for Damage Assessment of Structures using Electro-Mechanical Impedance Method
abstract: In this paper, we present a virtual instrumentation (VI) measurement system that measures the impedance of a piezoelectric transducer to detect the presence of damage using the electro-mechanical impedance (EMI) method. Thus, the measurement system can become a part of a structural health monitoring (SHM) system to determine the health of a structure. The measurement system consists of an analog interface circuit that uses a phase-sensitive rectifier (PSR) to measure the magnitude of the impedance of the piezo transducer, while the phase of the impedance of the transducer is determined using a phase measurement system (PMS) comprising of an exclusive-OR gate. A data acquisition system (DAQ) acquires the signals from the PSR and the PMS and is processed in a VI to access the damage. The key advantage of using this analog interface is it reduces the high sampling rate requirement of DAQ used in other measurement topologies, thereby reducing the cost of the overall measurement system. Experimental tests were conducted to evaluate the method’s effectiveness compared to conventional measurement systems, such as an LCR meter for a frequency range of 20 kHz to 35 kHz. A maximum deviation of 50 Ω was observed between the readings obtained from the LCR meter and the proposed method. By inducing damage using a steel nut placed at various distances from the transducer on a thin aluminum sheet, the proposed method was validated for its performance. The results demonstrated the system’s efficacy in measuring the impedance of a piezo-transducer for SHM applications.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Deep Learning Techniques on Classifying Commercial Sensor-based Auditory Brainstem Response
abstract: To objectively evaluate the health condition of the auditory pathway, Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR) is used in the clinic. The clinical diagnosis is concluded by the audiologist according to the morphology and characteristic waves of ABR through manual screening. It is a time-consuming and subjective task that not only reduces the efficiency of the physicians but also introduces subjective error which might cause an incorrect diagnosis. Therefore, it is necessary to propose an objective method that can solve the abovementioned problems. Deep Learning (DL) technique develops fast and is widely used in many fields, including biomedical engineering. Hence, DL might help with the objective classification of ABR and release the physicians from the heavy workload. In this paper, we evaluated the classification performance of three commonly used DL methods, namely EEGNet, DeepConvNet and ShallowConvNet, on several metrics. The results showed that on the task of classifying normal and abnormal ABR signals, EEGNet had the best performance, with the accuracy of 0.9995 ± 0.0011, the precision of 0.9995 ± 0.0011, the recall of 0.9995 ± 0.0011, the F1-score of 0.9995 ± 0.0011, and the AUC of 1.0000 ± 0.0000. It is believed that DL can help with objective ABR classification and release the physicians’ workload.

articleTitle: Smart Insole: A Wireless Gait Monitoring and Pressure Distribution Device
abstract: A wireless gait monitoring and pressure distributing device was successfully fabricated using copper sheet which was attached to a polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film using an adhesive. The fabricated device consisted of sixteen force sensitive resistors (FSR), three ESP32 microcontrollers. Calendering was performed to remove the wrinkles and air trapped in the copper traces to ensure good conductivity followed by lamination of the insole to avoid damage to FSRs, copper and preventing it from oxidizing. Smart insole was responsible for generating pressure and gait data on a computer application and provide the user feedback regarding the pressure applied on their foot. The performance of the device was investigated by measuring the force on each FSR using force gauge between 0 to 150 N of force with 10 N intervals in between the force. It was observed that the device demonstrated swift performance when and promptly sent data to the application while the subject was performing different strides such as heel strike, flat foot, mid stance, push off and, toe off.

articleTitle: In-situ Growth of the Co3O4 Laser Induced Graphene for Flexible Electronics Application
abstract: Emerging biodegradable and environmentally friendly technologies have the potential to change the futuristic landscape in the flexible electronics area. The paper-based substrates appear as a cost-effective and easily modifiable substance, making it a highly promising choice for flexible electronics. The incorporation of metal doping onto flexible substrates enhances the electrical, mechanical, and UV responsivity and sensitivity, thereby making them versatile for specific applications. This work introduces a modified paper with the in-situ growth of the Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> laser-induced graphene material that is suitable for flexible electronics applications. In this study, the developed material has been utilized and validated in three different applications, supercapacitor, touch sensor, and bending analysis.

articleTitle: Novel Cork-based Laser-Induced Graphene Sensors: Proof-of-Concept and Initial Results
abstract: The paper presents the fabrication and characterization of novel laser-induced Graphene (LIG)-based electrodes from cork substrates. The LIG has been a pioneering phenomenon for forming low-cost and robust sensors. Certain attributes like high electrical conductivity, high porosity, and easy synthesis process greatly increase the potential of LIG-based for electrochemical and strain-sensing applications. One of the challenges has been the formation of LIG from cheap, daily used objects to induce large-scale, low-cost graphene production. The initial characterization of LIG shown here forms a podium for developing multifunctional LIG-based sensors devised from cork substrates. Further experiments will be carried out and reported on optimizing the electro-mechanical characteristics of the LIG electrodes from cork substrates.

articleTitle: Finite element modelling of Graphene Gold Nanocomposite Coated Microchannels for Vitamin D Biosensor development
abstract: The proposed work is focused on investigating the theoretical simulation of the binding reaction kinetics of vitamin D immunoassay onto a graphene gold nanocomposite coated microchannels. In order to realize the binding reaction kinetics and identify the sensitivity of the immunoassay, chemical species transport module in COMSOL Multiphysics 5.5 is utilized. The optimum capture antibody concentration for yielding better sensitivity is studied using the association and dissociation reaction rate constants. The surface reactions are monitored and the sensitivity enhancement due to the graphene gold nanocomposites coated PMMA substrates is analyzed. From the simulation study, lower detection limits of 1 pM was achieved for detecting Vitamin D micronutrients present in blood which is much lower than the clinically significant levels. The study offers greater potential in understanding the theory behind affinity reaction of antibody and antigen which could be further extended for carrying out experiments towards vitamin D biosensor development. This could be vital for point of care sensing and act as a better screening tool in identifying the micronutrient deficiency particularly among women and children.

articleTitle: Short term demand forecasting using polynomial ARX models based on least squares methods
abstract: The article considers electrical power demand forecasting based on nonlinear ARX models. Polynomial ARX models are introduced as a kind of nonlinear ARX models. System identification problems of the polynomial ARX models are reduced to least squares problems using multiple input-output data if the nonlinear functions are assumed to be polynomial. A numerical example is shown to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method about short term demand forecasting in Tokyo.

articleTitle: BaTiO3 and Blue Phosphorus-MoS2/WS2 hybrid structure based Surface Plasmon Resonance sensor with improved sensing performance
abstract: A novel sensitivity enhanced surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is proposed based on BK7 prism, Silver (Ag), Barium titanate (BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and Blue Phosphorus-MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hybrid structure. The six layer SPR sensor is based on the Kretschmann angular interrogation method. The sensor utilizes BaTiO3 as an oxide layer over Ag film coated BK7 prism with a hybrid combination of Blue Phosphorus-MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> heterostructure and WS2. Transfer matrix method is used for the numerical analysis of the proposed sensor to investigate the SPR performance. The Sensitivity, Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) and Quality Factor (QF) of the sensor at an operating wavelength of 633nm is studied in the refractive index range 1.33-1.335 RIU. The thicknesses of the Ag, BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, BlueP-MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> heterostructure and WS2 layers are optimized to attain the highest sensitivity of 326°/RIU, FWHM and QF of 2.7534°and 118.4 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> respectively. The proposed sensor with 48nm Ag, 9nm BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, trilayers of BlueP-MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (2.25nm) and bilayers of WS2 (1.6nm) exhibits enhancement in the sensitivity and QF by 2.71 and 1.09 times over the conventional SPR sensor.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Micro-scaled Biosensor for Noninvasive Detection of Lactate
abstract: Lactate is a significant biomarker in the anaerobic metabolic pathways of the physiological system. The increase in the level of lactate may lead to disease conditions. It is an essential physical regulator. Lactate is detectable in a range of bodily fluids, such as blood, sweat, plasma, and urine. Among these choices, sweat demonstrates a notable level of concentration. Hence, the feasibility of noninvasive lactate detection has garnered increasing interest and offers a reassuring experience for patients. The present study focuses on the development of an electro-microfluidic device for the non-invasive detection of lactate. The detection platform utilizes an electrochemical sensing system as its foundation. An inkjet-printed electrode improved with multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNT) and functionalized with the Lactate oxidase (LO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) enzyme. The flexible microfluidic device integrated with a three-electrode system was used for electrochemical sensing lactate levels. The assessment of the enzyme immobilization response was conducted using cyclic voltammetry (CV). The sensor shows a linear range of 1-20 mM concentration with a limit of detection (LoD) and a Limit of Quantification (LoQ) as 1 mM and 3 mM. Due to the inherent flexibility of the electrode, it possesses the capability to be utilized for the purpose of point-of-care lactate detection.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of machine learning classifier on different cow health datasets
abstract: Animal welfare and good health are crucial for dairy cow farms and long-term milk production. Unfortunately, daily animal condition monitoring is challenging, especially on big farms where staff members need more time to observe animals and spot early signs of sickness. The machine learning algorithm can be constructive in continuously monitoring animal conditions. The performance of different classifiers is studied here, based on the CDAC-developed innovative farm-based cow health monitoring system. The system comprises hardware components, a cloud infrastructure, a client application, and cutting-edge data measurement and analysis algorithms. The device can successfully monitor animal well-being and the estrus cycle after being tested in a real-world setting. In this study, data was collected from the IMU sensor attached to the neck of the cows. Along with this manual data annotation, CCTV footage of the livestock was also recorded as a means of data verification. The help of machine learning algorithms, Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) to classify the behavior of the cattle were taken. The algorithms were used on datasets with different features, showing additional accuracy with the other featured datasets. A brief study was presented about the improvement and change in accuracy after using the machine learning algorithm on different datasets with different features.

articleTitle: Amplifying Proline Colorimetric Detection: A Frugal Approach for Paper based Biosensor
abstract: The point-of-care testing device has acquired importance for clinical diagnostics because of technological advances in resource-constrained situations and a decentralized healthcare system. The dependency on the point of care device is mainly due to sensitivity and specificity, caused by surface modifications, although it varies depending on several criteria. Our study generated silver nanoparticles using two different catalysts -CuSO4 and ZnSO4 (one parameter) via green synthesis and investigated their effect on the colorimetric detection of Animo acid: proline as a biosensing application and tested against antibacterial properties. A modified paper biosensor modified with catalyst CuS04 produces better results as compared to another for proline biosensing (LOD - 4.34 mM) and antibacterial application (1.8 cm long).

articleTitle: A Low Power DCOC Circuit with 57.7 dB DC-offset Attenuation for CW Radar Sensor
abstract: This article presents the design of a novel DC-offset cancellation (DCOC) circuit aimed to use in a homodyne continuous wave (CW) radar sensor receiver to overcome the leakage problem and is implemented in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS (Bipolar complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor). This is a resistor-less DCOC designed using a fully differential operational transconductance amplifier (OTA), feedback low-pass filter (LPF) realized using Miller’s multiplier-based capacitor with BJT for better DC-offset attenuation/cancellation and minimizing the layout area. The performance of this DCOC topology has been benchmarked through post-layout simulation results. This DCOC has demonstrated a DC-offset attenuation of 57.7 dB, DC-offset cancellation for the offset voltage varying from -0.3 V to 2 V, and noise figure (NF) from 20.3 dB to 26 dB in the pass-band frequency band of 3.98 KHz to 41 MHz. Compared to the available DCOC circuit in the literature, it has demonstrated the highest DC-offset attenuation and DC-offset cancellation by using the lowest power of 0.875 mW, and a layout area of 0.148 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Freshness Analysis of Orange using Bio-impedance Measurement and Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Assessing the quality of fruits after harvesting has become crucial to satisfy both production and consumer requirements. The freshness of fruits is measured with the help of various non-destructive methods to provide quality attributes without damaging their quality and texture. The utilization of computational techniques, such as Machine Learning (ML), is considered suitable for identifying physiological and bio/chemical modifications in fruit. This study employed the Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) technique to evaluate the freshness of the orange. The bio-impedance dataset was obtained for six days using the AD5933-based measurement setup. Various classification and regression-based ML algorithms were employed using MATLAB to predict the freshness of the orange. The ML classifiers and regressors were further evaluated based on their various performance indicators. In classification, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Neural Network (NN) demonstrated better performance for prediction. Whereas the NN regressor and Gaussian Process Regressor (GPR) algorithms exhibited better performance in precisely predicting the freshness of orange.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Wax Thickness in The Crude Oil Pipeline through IOT node-based system
abstract: The flow of crude oil through pipelines in the cold weather situation is profoundly affected because of the layers of the wax deposited on the inner surface of the pipelines. To sort out this problem, we proposed a technique which can detect and monitor the deposited wax thickness in the crude oil pipelines. The proposed technique has two different systems. The first system is used for the wax thickness measurement based on the change in the capacitance, and the second system is dedicated to the transmission of the measured wax information through IoT node globally. The experimental and simulated results are reported in this paper

articleTitle: Detection of Phosphate in water by using a planar pentagonal EME sensor for Agriculture Applications
abstract: The proposed sensor structure is able to generate electromagnetic field in the water sample containing phosphate, this field is used for sensing phosphate in water. The pentagonal shape electromagnetic sensor has a pentagon shape coil surrounding the interdigital capacitor. The electromagnetic field generated in the water sample causes a change in the impedance at the output of sensor that is equivalent to the concentration of phosphate. The sensor is modelled and simulated. These results are tested by experimentation. The behavioral characteristics of sensor were obtained in air and distilled water. The ammonium dihydrogen phosphate was added to distil water to form a solution. By varying the phosphate concentration in distilled water, the solutions were prepared. The sensor can differentiate the presence of phosphate. The sensor was immersed in the solution of various ppm and its responses were acquired. The simulation, experimental results and future improvements are also incorporated in the paper.

articleTitle: Graphene Oxide Blend for Advanced Sensing: A Nanocomposite Preparation and Comprehensive Characterization with Diverse Concentrations for Sensing Applications
abstract: This study presents the synthesis and comprehensive characterization of a Poly(methyl methacrylate)(PMMA) and Graphene oxide blend nanocomposite by chemical exfoliation, with a focus on its potential application as a sensing and absorbing material. The investigation involved formulating a GO/PMMA blend using a modified hummers method, incorporating two different concentrations of graphene oxide (GO) - 1% and 3% (wt.) - to tailor the desired properties. The resulting GO/PMMA composite was spincoated onto a silicon wafer substrate for acetone detection. Advanced techniques such as Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Xray diffraction (XRD), and Raman spectroscopy, Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) with Energy Dispersive X-ray (EDX) were employed for the comprehensive characterization of the nanocomposite. The results provided valuable insights into the characteristics of the GO/PMMA composite on Silicon wafer, opening avenues for the development of novel materials with potential applications in a wide range of fields.

articleTitle: Design, Modelling, and Simulation of PMUT Device for Ultrasound Imaging Applications
abstract: In this work, a circular piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) suitable for ultrasound imaging applications has been designed, modelled, and simulated using COMSOL™. The PMUT device uses Aluminum Nitride (AlN) as the piezoelectric material for achieving optimal performance. The resonant frequency, membrane displacement, and pressure-induced voltages have been studied. Moreover, a comparative study of circular, square and hexagonal geometries was also carried out to evaluate their impact on the eigenfrequency. Further, parametric sweeps are performed to study the influence of the radius and thickness of the piezoelectric layer on device performance. In addition, device performance was compared with Lead Zirconate Titanate (PZT) as the piezoelectric material. The simulation results show a resonant frequency of 7.7511 MHz and a maximum membrane displacement of 0.228 µm at the resonant frequency, while pressure-induced voltage reaches 0.292 V/mN. The parametric studies show that resonant frequency decreases when increasing the radius of the diaphragm while it increases when the piezoelectric layer’s thickness increases. Moreover, the resonant frequency of AlN-PMUT was higher than PZT-PMUT for various geometries. The results have been verified using an analytical model developed on MATLAB™.

articleTitle: Solution Processable β-Gallium oxide for Application in Solar-Blind UV Detectors
abstract: Solar-Blind UV detection systems are not affected by the background radiation noise from the sun, which makes them attractive for applications in environmental monitoring and defense systems. Colloidally grown gallium oxide (Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) nanoparticles are investigated for their application in solar-blind UV detectors. The synthesis temperature is maintained at a growth temperature of 250°C. Long chain organic capping molecules are employed to control size and structure of the nanopartilces and to render them dispersible in a solvent for device fabrication. The bandgap is found to be 4.82eV from the excitonic peak of the absorbance spectrum. These nanoparticles are also highly crystalline as seen from the X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements with a cyrstallite size of 20nm. The presence of Beta-phase Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is established from the different modes seen on the Raman spectrum.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of MEMS-based Thermopile Detector Arrays for Infrared Sensing Applications
abstract: This research focuses on MEMS thermopile-based arrays. Thermopile-based detectors employ the Seebeck effect to generate electrical potential differences in response to temperature variations. The thermopiles are composed of polysilicon-based thermocouple elements interconnected in arrays to enhance sensitivity and output voltage.Expanding upon the prior work involving a double-layer structure and a single-layer circular structure, our research explores various thermocouple designs more comprehensively. This includes parametric variations of length and thickness and the development of stacked double-layer structure and its subsequent implementation in a circular array . In our study, we delve into crucial factors such as doping concentration, polysilicon layer thickness, and insulating silicon dioxide layer thickness to engineer specific Seebeck coefficients and achieve enhanced output voltage.Our findings reveal an important trend: increasing doping concentration reduces the Seebeck coefficient, while decreasing thermocouple strip thickness improves the output voltage. Minimizing the oxide layer thickness also proves instrumental in increasing the output voltage.Additionally, circular arrays are examined to analyze their performance in different thermoelectric structures. Through comparative analysis, the device performance in circular arrays for single-layer, double-layer, and stacked double-layer thermopile structures is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A shape memory alloy spring actuated gripper with self-sensing feedback for control
abstract: This article suggests a self-sensing gripper that is driven by a single Shape memory alloy (SMA) spring to enable precise self-sensing. The gripper that is in normally open mode consists of two arms, one of which is fixed and an SMA spring actuator controls the other. This article demonstrates that the variation in the resistance of the shape memory alloy spring reveals phase transitions and can be used to detect the position of the gripper arm, enabling position control. The development of self-sensing technology broadens the concept of gripper sensing, which helps to advance compactness and miniaturization. This work suggests the design, manufacture, and characterization of a gripper that gives the benefit of sensorless position control.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Microfluidic Chip for Temperature Control Applications in Biomedical
abstract: This paper proposes an On-chip microfluidic system specially designed for temperature control reactions in biomedical, for example, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) applications. The microfluidic chip and thin film heaters have been designed using COMSOL Multiphysics. The proposed system is fabricated on a glass substrate of size 5×5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, taking advantage of the thermally conductive and electrically insulating substrate. The microfluidic system made in Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) consists of a reaction chamber for PCR, a microchannel for fluid handling, and two thermally actuated valves for fluid control. On the other side of the glass substrate, it has three thin film metal heaters made in Cr/Al/Cr layers which are intergraded with the microfluidic network over the glass substrate. The middle heater is used for performing PCR reactions and the left and right heaters are fabricated for the actuation of valves. Therefore, the channel can be closed, and the PCR chamber can become isolated for the reaction to take place. However, after closing the channel, the shape mismatching between the rectangular cross-section of the channel and the balloon-shaped valve membrane (after actuation) results in the sample's leakage. Therefore, after some time the reaction chamber becomes empty which leads to the device failure. To overcome this issue, a semicircular cross-section PDMS channel has also been made using the AZ 40 XT positive photoresist mold. The fabricated microfluidic network has been integrated with the thin film heaters over the glass substrate using the different thin and thick film technological steps. Finally, the system has been tested for further verification of leakage from the microfluidic channel.

articleTitle: Ultrasound based Gas Detection: Analyzing Acoustic Impedance for High-Performance and Low-Cost Solutions
abstract: Gas leakage is a serious hazard in a variety of sectors, including industrial, domestic, and gas-powered vehicles. The installation of gas leak detection systems has emerged as a critical preventative measure to solve this problem. Traditional gas sensors, such as electrochemical, infrared point, and Metal Oxide Semiconductor sensors, have been widely used for gas leak detection. However, these sensors have limitations in terms of their adaptation to various gases, as well as their high cost and difficulties in scaling. In this paper, a novel non-contact gas detection technique based on a 40 kHz ultrasonic signal is described. The proposed approach employs the reflections of the emitted ultrasonic wave to detect the gas leaks and also able to identify the exact gas in real-time. To confirm the method’s effectiveness, trials were carried out using Hydrogen, Helium, Argon, and Butane gas. The system identified gas flow breaches in 0.01 seconds, whereas the gas identification procedure took 0.8 seconds. An interesting extension of the proposed approach is real-time visualisation of gas flow employing an array of transducers.

articleTitle: Measurement of Parameters of BLDC Motor under Various Conditions for Autonomous Vehicles Applications
abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors find extensive application across diverse fields due to their versatility. Consequently, the imperative to enhance their performance becomes paramount. To achieve this objective, a thorough measurement of their operational parameters under varying working conditions is indispensable as it lays the foundation for potential improvements. Accordingly, this research endeavors to investigate the performance of multiple BLDC motors and drivers through rigorous experimentation. The measurements include crucial parameters such as motor input current, input voltage, motor phase current, rotational speed, and force output, facilitated by the incorporation of requisite sensors. The findings from these experiments are of substantial significance for subsequent stages in motor optimization, providing valuable insights to enhance their operational efficiency and effectiveness in practical applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Photoacoustic Sensing System for Expeditive Estimation of Paint’s Viscosity
abstract: Non-invasive and rapid measurement of paint's viscosity is a challenge for most of the paint manufacturing industries. This study proposes a novel photoacoustic (PA) sensing technique for the measurement of paint's viscosity. The continuous wave laser diode used in an excitation makes the overall system compact and portable. The application of the sweep frequency acoustic interferometry principle enhances the signal to noise ratio of the PA signal. The paint samples are mixed with a thinner solution to vary their viscosity. Zahn-4 cup is used to measure the viscosity of the paint samples which acts as the ground truth. A regression-based analysis is performed to estimate the viscosity through PA measurements. Viscosity measured through PA is compared with the ground truth and the error found is approximately less than 5%. The simple computational method and instrumentation used in this technique enable it to be deployed in industries for rapid estimation of the viscosity of paints.

articleTitle: Valvular Heart Disease Prediction Using CNN-based Residual Network
abstract: For decades, the cardiovascular disease which is also known as coronary artery disease, acts on the heart and has been recognized as the preeminent invoke of disease. Heart diseases is among the most severe diseases, and it impacts a lot of people all around the world. Early detection of heart illness may result in its prevention or amelioration, which may lower mortality rates. The proposed study used different heart disease datasets and deep learning techniques for classification. Deep learning (DL) can deliver a powerful answer for decision-making and correct predictions of valvular heart diseases. Early prediction of coronary heart disorder may also store many people’s lives; detecting cardiovascular illnesses like coronary heart attacks, coronary artery illness, etc., is a reproving task using ordinary scientific analysis. Feature extraction and classification techniques of heart sound provide a better way of study of phonocardiography (PCG) signal analysis which eventually reduces the cost, makes the system compact, and at the same time, can work with big data. This paper mainly has two segments feature extraction and classification. In feature extraction section, time domain features, statistical features, and acoustic features are used. For the classification of heart sound, the proposed CNN-based Residual Network is used. The CNN-based network is very effective in heart sound analysis, requiring much less computation time. The proposed CNN-based model scored an accuracy of 97.04 ±0.05 % on the test dataset with a sensitivity of 96.8 ± 0.03 % and specificity of 96.2 ± 0.04%.

articleTitle: Resolution Improvement in wearable E-skin for large area robotic
abstract: This study proposes a novel method for enhancing E-skin resolution for wearable large area robotic applications. In order to perform delicate manipulation, object recognition, and secure human-robot interactions, it is essential for robots to have finer tactile discriminating capabilities, which is addressed in this study. The proposed methodology achieves a significant improvement in the resolution of e-skin by utilizing novel sensor mesh architecture and signal processing techniques.This paper proposes a mesh architecture with significant increase in the density of tactile electrodes featuring wearable E- skin through a thorough set of studies. Robotic systems ability to distinguish tiny features and textures on a variety of surfaces is significantly improved by this augmentation, in combination with sophisticated sensor configurations and accuracy improvements using LLM algorithms.The results of this study have important ramifications for a variety of applications, including interactive humanoid robotics, healthcare, manufacturing, and rehabilitation. Industries that depend on robots for activities demanding great precision and adaptability in dynamic situations could be revolutionized by the E-skin technology.

articleTitle: Material Classification and Accuracy Testing Using Passive CRFID Transponder in Recycle Unit
abstract: Inappropriate material management in recycling chains lead to adverse effects of metals and glass inoculation in the plastic-only recyclable units/chains. Despite multiple ways to sort out plastic materials in garbage bins and large scale recycle units, intensive efforts are still needed to map the high cost and optic/light sensors drawbacks. In this paper, we propose a low-cost passive solution to the problem via design and deployment of smart wireless IoT sensor for material identification in huge recycle units. The sensor tag comprises of multi-resonator and slot structure yielding multiple bit response in maximum of 4.3mm radial dimensions. The electromagnetic radar cross section (EM RCS) signature is evaluated at three unique notches 21.4GHz, 23.7GHz, and 27.8GHz frequency, containing 3-unique data bits. The tag is designed using semi-octagonal structure to generate 3-bit EM signature. The resonance frequency and RCS response of tag is analyzed using CST Studio Suit software at far-field distance via incident plain wave. The approach is how accurately the plastic type and other materials are sorted out using single battery-free tag. As proof-of-concept, multiple samples of glass, metals and plastic type-1 and plastic type-2 are tested in the set-up for material classification. PET is used as plastic type-1 and HDPE is used as plastic type-2 material. Whereas, Aluminum is used as metal material, while soda lime material is used for glass classification. By deployment of presented smart sensor in commercial recycling chains/units, this concept can be utilized at huge market level for recycle applications, leading to a hygienic community excelled in all aspects of health safety.

articleTitle: Dielectrically Modulated Junctionless Rectangular Gate All Around FET based Biosensor for Label Free detection of Neutral Biomolecules
abstract: In this work, a dielectric-modulated rectangular gate-all-around junctionless field effect transistor (DMRGAA-JLT) has been designed for detection of neutral biomolecules present in human body. Various electrical parameter like-Surface Potential, Drain Current, transconductance etc are explored to investigate the sensitivity of the proposed biosensor. The proposed device is explored and optimized for two cavities i.e.100 nm & 150 nm. The proposed biosensor has no source & drain junctions hence, it is easy to fabricate. Due to bulk conduction, less short channel effect occurs in it. Various biomolecules such as Streptavidin, APTES, Zein, Keratin are immobilized in the cavity and remarkable changes has occurred on the sensitivity of the device. The proposed biosensor shows better sensitivity for cavity length of 150nm. Maximum ON current 7.27 X 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> A, maximum drain current 6.88 X 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> A and transconductance 2.12 X 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> µA/V is achieved. Furthermore, it is implied that the sensitivity of the biosensor increases with increase in cavity length. The proposed biosensor is also compared with BP-JLFET, DM-FET and DM-TFET for drain current sensitivity and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> ratio. The results shows that JL-RGAA-FET exhibits better sensitivity as compared to BP-JLFET, DM-FET and DM-TFET.

articleTitle: Capacitance based MEMS Microphone for point of care application to monitor ascultations
abstract: In this paper, the design and simulation of MEMS microphone for the sound pressure range of 116 µPa- 1Pa which corresponds to the heart auscultation range of 20 to 60 dB Sound Pressure Level (SPL) is presented [1]. It is analyzed for the functionality to be applicable as point of care application to mediate auscultations. Microphone’s design consists of two parallel conductive plates separated by a distance of 2µm and a frame of insulator made out of silicon dioxide. The thickness of the diaphragm is 1.5µm with diameter 800µm. There are c-shaped slots incorporated at the top surface of the diaphragm of size 10µm to ensure maximum deflection and thus to increase the capacitance [2]. The Microphone was simulated and compared in ANSYS and COMSOL to estimate the range of various parameters such as, displacement, stress, modal and electromechanical analysis.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Wireless Sensor Networks with Multi-state Nodes
abstract: Today's era of Internet of Things have seen automation in almost every field including agriculture. Implementation of rovers in the agricultural sector has brought a tremendous socio-economic impact. These rovers along with other field-deployed sensors forms a network that encourages complete automated monitoring of the agricultural field. Therefore, it has become very essential to quantify the performability of such a network. Due to its hardware architecture and environmental effects, at any point of time the components of the rovers may not function properly. As such, the rover may exist in ACTIVE, DEGRADED, RELAY or FAILURE state. To quantify the performance of such networks with multistate rovers, and multistate sensors, this paper proposes a reliability evaluation approach that utilizes a distance, and energy matrix to find the connectivity between the field deployed sensors, rovers and the data collector(s). The proposed approach uses Monte Carlo simulation to evaluate reliability. The proposed approach is illustrated through a series of examples.

articleTitle: Planar Hexagonal Sensor for Phosphate detection
abstract: This paper describes the development of a six-planar electromagnetic hexagonal sensor, which consists of a hexagonal spiral coil, an inductor, and an interdigital capacitor. The magnetic field produced by the inductor hexagonal coil and the electric field produced by the inter-digital capacitor combine to form an electromagnetic field. The hexagonal shape Spiral coils have three, four, and five turns. The sensor has been tested at frequencies ranging from 50Hz to 200 KHz. The impedance variation of all sensors in air is used to determine their sensor properties. The sensors are tested in distilled water. The ammonium-dehydrate-phosphate is mixed with distilled water and the different concentration were used to test the sensor selectivity and sensitivity.

articleTitle: Smartphone-Based Road Condition Monitoring: A Feasibility Study
abstract: Driving safety, riding quality and fuel efficiency are heavily influenced by the surface conditions and structural integrity of roads, and the World Bank has identified it as one of the main factors in the analysis of road quality vs. user cost. This paper presents a proof-of-concept study on monitoring road conditions by analyzing the data in smartphones placed inside the backpacks of cyclists. We demonstrate by experimentation and data analysis techniques that it is feasible to obtain valuable information on the condition of roads from smartphones placed inside the backpacks of cyclists, including the assignment of acceleration signatures to specific irregularities and anomalies on the surface of roads, such as bumps and manholes. Moreover, this preliminary investigation shows the tremendous potential portable, mobile sensing platforms have in many future long-term applications such as the internet-of-things, urban mobility, digital twins and smart cities.

articleTitle: Development of Electrode Polarization Impedance based Bubble Detection in Flow Channels
abstract: This paper presents the development of an electrode polarization impedance concept as detection principle of bubble in flow channel. Bubble detection techniques are essential for safety, quality control, process optimization, and advancing scientific understanding. They enable efficient operations, improve product quality, and contribute to advancements in various industries and research fields. By monitoring the electrode polarization impedance change, the sensor can detect the presence of the bubble. The magnitude of the generated signals is influenced by several factors, including the bubble size, the exposed area of the electrode in the solution, the position of contact between the bubble and the electrode, and the concentrations of ions in the solution. Additionally, this system can serve as a multifunctional sensor, capable of measuring the flow rate of conductivity and detecting bubbles within flow channels.

articleTitle: Development of Autonomous Robot To Perform Multiple Tasks in Agricultural Fields
abstract: Robotics and mechatronics have been used in many arenas, one of which is the agricultural industry. Using robotic-based machines in agriculture will become common in the future. However, these machines are not affordable for farmers in a country like India. This creates a need of developing a low-cost multi-tasking robot to work in agricultural fields. An attempt has been made to develop such a robot that can greatly help farmers to achieve efficient farming. The robot can perform four modes of operation. One is the navigation of the robot based on a defined path provided by the user. The Second mode of operation is acquiring the data on moisture, temperature, pH level, and NPK (nitrogen, potassium, and Calcium) level of the soil. The third mode of operation is digging the soil and plantation of the seeds or saplings and the final mode is sprinkling of water as per the soil condition. The device is designed, constructed, and validated on the laboratory scale with considerable accuracy.

articleTitle: Microscaled Electrochemiluminescence System for High-Throughput Visual Detection of H2O2
abstract: The presented work aims to provide insights into developing single-electrode electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensors for high throughput detection of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Herein, an Indium tin oxide-single electrode ECL (ITO-SE-ECL) platform was fabricated using the photolithography technique to leverage the benefits of good electrical and optical transparency of ITO for ECL-based visual imaging. This system includes cathode and anode electrodes in a microfluidic chamber. The emitted ECL signal, due to luminol oxidation on the anode, was monitored to determine the hydrogen peroxide (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) concentration. The static interaction between the ECL-emitted signal of Luminol on the ITO electrode was also studied under optimized assay parameters. The proposed biosensor can be applied as a promising alternative method for the indirect detection of various human metabolites.

articleTitle: Multi-depth Capacitive Soil Sensor Node Testing and Deployment
abstract: With the advent of Agriculture 4.0 which encompasses cutting-edge technologies such as smart sensors, robots, wireless networks, big data analytics, machine learning, and much more. These advanced technologies allow agronomists and meteorologists to make profitable and environmentally friendly decisions. In recent times, several sensing methods have been developed to acquire soil moisture data. However, the studies exhibited severe limitations in terms of effectiveness and reliability. The current work presents the development and real field testing of a low-cost multi-depth capacitive soil sensor node that is capable of communicating real-time field data with high spatial resolution and scalability. The sensors are tested and calibrated in the lab before being trialed at a real pilot farm. The proposed sensor node also employed a tipping rain sensor and an environmental sensor to enhance the overall understanding of land and climatic conditions. The preliminary findings from the field sensors showed promising results that can be effectively utilized for long-term applications such as irrigation scheduling and weather forecasting. Such a system with industry collaboration can be considered a cost-effective solution for expensive commercial tools.

articleTitle: Numerical study to assess the compatibility of polymer materials as a substrate for MEMS based flexible flow sensor
abstract: By virtue of their small size, increased efficiency and performance arising from scaling effect, the Micro-Electromechanical Systems (MEMS) have become very popular in the biomedical industry in recent years. MEMS-based flexible flow sensor is one such device. An optimized MEMS-based flexible flow sensor is proposed in this study to improve the technology which will help to diagnose cardiovascular diseases with greater accuracy. Different polymer materials for the substrate were explored and were filtered first based on their bio-compatibility. Subsequently, a numerical study on COMSOL Multiphysics was performed to get a suitable material combination that uses lower power consumption for the same temperature rise (∆T) as that of our reference combination which comprises Poly-Dimethly-Siloxane (PDMS) as substrate and nichrome as heater; or has less stress induced upon heating. Temperature rise of 6K for Polyvinylchloride (PVC) as substrate and nichrome as heater at 3.9 V was achieved which is less than 4.2 V of reference combination. Also, the same temperature rise was observed in Polyimide as that of PDMS, both at 4.2 V with less internal stresses.

articleTitle: Low-cost paper-based sensors for strain-induced applications
abstract: The paper presents the work done on the fabrication and implementation of low-cost, dip-coated sensors for tactile applications. Graphene nanoparticles and tissue papers were used as raw materials to form the sensors. The prototypes were encapsulated with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) to make them tear and wear resistant. Graphene has been one of the pioneering materials in forming flexible, conductive prototypes. The prototypes were formed using dip-coating process, which has been one widely used synthesis technique due to advantages like customization of layer thickness, quick batch production and ability to process a wide range of nanomaterials and polymers. The results shown here provides a proof-of-concept and forms a podium to use these sensors for multiple strain-induced applications.

articleTitle: Process Optimisation in Real-Time Domains Using Microcontroller-Based Sensor Devices
abstract: Life and property are threatened by emergencies that occur in real-time domains with disastrous consequences. It is often the result of a poor awareness of precursors to the event. Such situations cause health issues, fire safety incidents, traffic accidents, negligence and even opportunistic criminality. Managing potential disasters in real-time relies significantly on credible edge intelligence (i.e., knowledge derived from analysed remote event data). Our research presents new methods, techniques and technologies to extract relevant data pre, during and post-event. Early precursor detection and response techniques reduce calamitous occurrences and the threat of emergencies in real-time domains.We demonstrate how microcontroller onboard sensors are "active" and can be tailored to perform effectively in changing, demanding, time-constrained operating environments. They replace passive standard procedural logic with machine learning multifactor associations to improve detection performance "at the edge". We show how "active" sensory capability and relevant data analysis make it possible to extract insights on precursors to manage situational risks more effectively. We discover why and how detecting and recognising a real-time incident's severity is critical to delivering the correct response. The research also uses data from diverse trial location scenarios and data types to improve risk assessment techniques in the targeted real-time domains. Using analysed "site data", we demonstrate how edge intelligence makes it possible to get early warning of events never ordinarily observed before. We have devised a "learning sensor" environment that improves the capability to "predict" and respond to new scenarios that threaten life and property.

articleTitle: Indoor Air Quality(IAQ) assessment using Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) for Multi-Storey Building Residents
abstract: This paper introduces a groundbreaking embedded platform designed for the comprehensive assessment of indoor air quality within multi-story buildings. The key innovation lies in the integration of an array of cost-effective sensors in every room, forming a novel hybrid sensing node for data collection. The wireless sensor network employs ZigBee protocol to establish a mesh network throughout the entire building, ensuring seamless coverage of all relevant areas without relying on a local area network. This novel wireless sensor network comprises a diverse set of sensors, encompassing CO2, CO, VOC, temperature, and humidity sensors, complemented by routers for long-range network propagation across multiple floors, as well as a coordinator for seamless computer communication. The uniqueness of this work extends further as it presents a fully functional prototype that has been rigorously tested, generating real-time air quality monitoring data through the innovative use of the Node-red application. To push the boundaries even further, the captured data is subjected to analysis using a sophisticated multilayer perceptron model. This model enables precise air quality assessment and prediction, contributing significantly to the field of air quality monitoring.

articleTitle: A Novel Home Energy Management System (HEMS) for Peak Load Reduction using LabVIEW
abstract: Energy management and conservation is increasingly becoming relevant in today’s world of climate change and scarcity of resources. Residential households consume a significant percent of the total power consumption. In India the growing number of residential households has often pushed the power consumption even to its peak at certain times of a day during which shoots challenges for utilities to maintain demand-supply balance. That in turn make invest more capital in purchasing of power at higher costs. This work proposes a new energy management algorithm for residential houses during peak hours so as to attain the goals of power and cost savings. The proposed Home Energy Management System (HEMS) algorithm was implemented using LabVIEW simulation model. The results show that there is a huge potential opportunity for effective residential load management with significant energy saving that in turn reduces the cost for both consumer and utilities. With the considered load conditions, the work produces 61% of energy savings.

articleTitle: Self-Controlled Robust Digital Readout Circuit for Resistance Measurement: Enhancing Immunity to Circuit Nonidealities
abstract: This paper proposes a self-controlled digital readout circuit for resistance measurement. The circuit offers numerous advantages, such as independence from circuit nonidealities, the elimination of the need for a control unit, a wide range of measurements, etc. Mathematical proofs are provided within the paper to demonstrate these benefits. The performance of the circuit is validated through simulation and an extensive experimental study. The results reveal a maximum nonlinearity of 0.2 % and a relative error of 0.4 % for the proposed circuit. Additionally, a comparative study is conducted to compare the results and advantageous features of the proposed circuit with those of existing digital readout circuits. Through various analyses, it is determined that the proposed circuit outperforms the existing alternatives. As a result, the proposed circuit is highly recommended for near-sensor applications.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Estimation using Four-probe Electrical Impedance Plethysmography
abstract: In this paper, a simple instrumentation platform, based on four-probe electrical impedance plethysmography, has been designed and evaluated. The proposed system provides a non-invasive method to acquire bio-impedance signals and thereby, estimate the heart-rate information. The bioimpedance measurement system proposed in this paper consists of three subsystems namely, the current excitation subsystem, voltage acquisition subsystem and signal processing subsystem. Four bio-electrodes are placed on the forearm, where the current is driven through the two outermost electrodes and voltage across the innermost electrodes is measured and processed to obtain the impedance plethysmography (IPG) signals. Simple electronic stages for this electrode system has been carefully designed and systematically evaluated. The proposed system has been tested on 10 humans, 3 trials each. The maximum error of the system in estimating the heart rate is 2 beats per minute (bpm). The proposed technique serves as an alternative to current HR estimation techniques by providing continuous HR monitoring along with portability.

articleTitle: A Miniaturised Electrochemical Platform for Rapid Detection of Insulin
abstract: The development of biosensors has revolutionized medical diagnostics and healthcare monitoring. Integration of nanomaterials, such as gold nano-islands (Au NIs), enhances the performance of electrochemical biosensors by increasing the active sites for biomolecular reception and the transduction of binding events into electrical signals. Insulin detection is critically required for automated type 1 diabetes management. Here, we report an aptamer-based electrochemical biosensor design for the rapid, sensitive, and selective detection of insulin. Au NIs are deposited on screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCEs) using a flame-based aerosol approach. The Au NIs are functionalised with an insulin-specific DNA aptamer, and the residual sensor surface is passivated with 6-mercapto-1-hexanol and bovine serum albumin. Our biosensor exhibits a linear response to insulin concentrations from 1 to 100 µM and demonstrates excellent selectivity for insulin as tested against glycine, glucose, ampicillin, glycated and non-glycated human serum albumin. Our biosensor's performance is validated in spiked mice serum exhibiting high recovery rates, thereby indicating its sensitivity and accuracy in real clinical scenarios. The selectivity of this biosensor is also assessed in mice serum to further emphasise on its clinical potential, demonstrating the potential for point-of-care diagnostics, wearable health monitoring devices, and personalised medicine for diabetes management.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of Micro-blowers for the design of Micro Automatic Positive Airway Pressure System for Obstructive Sleep Apnea Treatment
abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a condition, in which during the sleep the upper airway is obstructed due to the throat muscles relaxation. The conventional systems used for treatment of OSA are Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and Automatic positive airway pressure (APAP) devices which deliver required air pressure to open the airway obstruction. The major drawback of these systems is the presence of tubing that tangles around the patient’s neck causing discomfort and curbs the freedom of sleep position during sleep. This research work aims at analysing and selecting Micro-Electro-Mechanical System (MEMS) based micro-blowers for the design of an APAP system. It is planned to design a hoseless APAP system which embeds the APAP system within a face mask. Five different micro blowers such as Murata MZB1001T02, Delta BSB01703HA300CAJ, TF029B-1000F, TF037F-2000F, Sunon UB5U3-700 have been identified based on weight, flow rate, pressure and operating voltage. The performance metrics such as air pressure, flow specifications, current and power consumption of these 5 different micro-blowers are analysed for the effective use in the hoseless APAP system. Two micro-blowers namely, TF029B-1000F and UB5U3-700 were found to deliver the required pressure and air flow as per the conventional APAP systems. TF029B micro-blowers were used for the design of hoseless APAP device as it weighs less compared to TF037F micro-blower. This hoseless APAP device does not disturb the patients when changing their sleep position. It is acting as a user comfortable sleep aiding device compared to existing CPAP/APAP devices available in the market.

articleTitle: Charge-Discharge-Based Digitizer for Resistive Displacement Sensor
abstract: Resistive transducers offer a simple, low-cost and easy-to-use method for displacement sensing. Given these features, resistance-based displacement sensors are widely used in a number of industrial applications. This paper presents a simple microcontroller-based digitizer, employing a novel charge and discharge technique, for accurate digitization of a resistive displacement sensor. The proposed digitizer utilizes just two conversion cycles to convert the input displacement into a digital format. As opposed to most of the existing digitizers that uses a preset charging duration, the proposed scheme wisely configures and employs charging periods to extract information related to the measurement process. The output of the scheme is also independent of pin resistances and internal reference voltages. The paper brings out the working principle and performance validation of the presented scheme. Experimental studies show that the developed scheme can give good performance when interfaced with a commercial displacement sensor, and the worst-case error observed is 0.18 %. The proffered solution can serve as a cost-effective and efficient digitizing solution for capturing shaft displacements.

articleTitle: Enzymatic Biofuel cell with Silver-leaf Bioelectrodes for Energy Harvesting from Glucose
abstract: The performance and properties of the silver leaf enzymatic biofuel cell are ideal for use with various power sources. The corner of the silver electrode region, the silver leaf attached to a double-sided (10 mm × 10 mm) adhesive tape, and the electrical connections will all be visible with copper tape. In a range of operating modes, including cyclic voltammetry (CV), linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), and chronoamperometry (CA), the electrode that was intended to function as both an anode and a cathode performed as anticipated. These methodologies were applied for the efficiency assessment. This disposable electrode configuration can withstand an open-circuit voltage of 300 mV and generate an 84 μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> power density. This innovative method makes it possible to use inexpensive electrodes in microelectronic devices in a flexible manner.

articleTitle: Design and Investigation of PMUT Sensor for Rangefinding Applications
abstract: This work presents a study on the design and investigation of Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers (PMUTs), which can be utilised in rangefinding applications. In this work, we have designed a PMUT cell in which the piezoelectric material is Aluminium Nitride (AlN). Its performance was simulated using COMSOL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> and verified using an analytical model developed in MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup>. Studies were also conducted to determine the device's resonant frequency and how it varied with parameters such radius of the diaphragm, thickness of the piezoelectric layer and thickness of the active layer of SOI wafer, for different piezoelectric materials. The obtained eigenfrequency for circular diaphragm PMUT is 207.17 kHz. It was observed that eigenfrequency reduces as the diaphragm radius increases, while it increases with the thickness of the piezoelectric layer and active layer. The displacement of the membrane on applying an electric potential and the voltage generated on applying a force were studied as well. A hexagonal geometric variation of the device was also studied taking into consideration the increased packing efficiency.

articleTitle: Membraneless 3D printed Fiber-Based Microbial Fuel Cells harnessing Pseudomonas Aeuroginosa for Energy Production
abstract: Fiber-based Microbial Fuel Cells (MFCs) are emerging as promising technology in the field of fuel cells. Due, to the features like its inexpensive nature, naivety in fabrication, and its abundance of availability they manifest an upper edge over the other fluidic-based MFCs. Fiber-based MFCs are the epitome of an electrochemical system that uses bacteria for power generation and wastewater treatment in the paper substrate. Fiber-based miniaturized devices have gained significant attention over the last few years due to their flexible application in medical science, biosensors, etc. This work fabricated paper-based miniaturized MFCs using a 3D printer. Carbon Cloth was used as the working electrode and Pseudomonas Aeruginosa (Pseudomonas A) as the fuel to generate power. A comparative study showed that the fiber treated in oxygen plasma showed an optimized power output of around 345.40 µW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a current output of 20.95 µA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Fluorescence-based Detection of Uric Acid and Iron using Novel Carbon Nanodots
abstract: Abnormal level of uric acid is associated with certain biomedical implications such as gout, Alzheimer’s, multiple sclerosis, and renal failure, among others. Furthermore, there have been reports of the association between iron (III) and uric acid levels, and simultaneous detection could be crucial to managing or preventing further health complications. In this work, we focus on designing novel carbon nanodots [also called carbon dots (CDs)] for the detection of both the target analyte, i.e., uric acid and iron (III). We developed sulfur, nitrogen-co-doped carbon dots (S, N-co-doped-CDs) that emit blue fluorescence, and it was found that uric acid (UA) and iron (III) quenched the fluorescence when excited at 390nm and 360nm, respectively. Through this fluorescence-based simultaneous detection approach, the limit of detection of UA and Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> were found to be 96.32 μM and 0.13 mM, respectively. This suggests the potential of synthesized CD for the simultaneous detection of Uric acid and Iron (III), specifically in the development of optical-based biosensors.

articleTitle: Advancing Nitrite Sensing: A Comparative Study of Graphene and Carbon-Based PLA 3D Printed Electrochemical Sensors
abstract: Employment of Fused deposition modelling (FDM) as a sensor presents an opportunity to fabricate and develop sensors at a mass scale with good reproducibly as reduces or eliminates human intervention, hence, lesser error. In this work a conductive graphene and carbon based polylactic acid (PLA) filaments were used to 3D printed devices for electrochemical sensing of the nitrite. The limit of detection was 1.08 μM and 1.89 μM for the graphene and proto-pasta PLA respectively along with specific response for the nitrite.

articleTitle: Design optimization of trident shaped micro channels on paper for multiplex detection
abstract: This paper studies the various designs of paper-based device to optimize the flow rate for the purpose of multiplexed detection of biomarkers. In this study, four different trident-shaped designs were investigated based on sample volume and flow time optimization. The selection of optimized design was performed based on minimum time for the flow of minimum sample volume. The optimization results show that the most optimal flow time was 20s with an optimized sample volume of 4µl, which was demonstrated by the channel design tapered at an angle of 20°. Further, theoretical analysis was also performed with COMSOL-based simulation analysis to investigate the optimized design module for the trident-shaped microchannel geometry over the paper substrate.

articleTitle: Hardware Deployable Classifier for Invasive Ductal Carcinoma using Tiny Machine Learning Model
abstract: Breast Cancer is a global health concern, emphasizing the crucial importance of its early detection in improving patient treatment. This is especially true for the most frequently diagnosed type of breast cancer, Invasive Ductal Carcinoma (IDC), which has a high risk of spreading and significant mortality. Automation provides an opportunity to streamline the detection, improving efficiency and minimizing diagnostic errors. In this research paper, we proposed a low-computational Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) model for the classification of IDC. Conventional methods for IDC classification, such as histopathological analysis and mammography, are time-consuming, costly, and subjective. Therefore, there is a need for an automated and accurate method for IDC classification that can be applied in a resource-limited environment. Our proposed TinyML model takes digital images of whole-mount breast cancer slide specimens and extracts the features necessary to classify them as IDC-(-ve) or IDC-(+ve). The TinyML model is evaluated using a publicly available dataset of Breast Histopathology Images and compared to the other Deep Learning (DL) models based on accuracy and computational complexity. The results show that our model achieved a high accuracy of 89.3% while maintaining limited processing power and memory. The successful deployment of the model on an embedded system like Raspberry Pi demonstrates that our TinyML model can be used in hardware resource- constrained environments, promising improved cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: Fully Flexible Polyimide - Thermoplastic Polyurethane Based Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Energy Harvesting Applications
abstract: We report a simple fabrication, great performance and cost-effective triboelectric nanogenerator, which is based on a flexible vertical contact-separation mode based triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG). The TENG was fabricated using screen printing processes. Polyimide (PI) materials was used as a tribo-negative layer and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) was used as tribo-positive layer. The electrodes for TENG was fabricated by screen printing Ag ink on a flexible TPU and polyimide (PI) substrates for scavenging mechanical energy into electrical energy. The performance of the TENG was demonstrated by investigating the open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current and instantaneous consumed power on the resistive loads. It was observed that the open-circuit voltage was stabilized at 22 V with a short-circuit current of 12 µA. To demonstrate the vertical contact induced energy harvesting ability, the fabricated TENG device was attached to the shoe sock and shoe sole to harvest the energy from human motion.

articleTitle: A Digital Twin Approach for Estimation of Contaminants in Lubrication Oil through Photoacoustic Sensing System
abstract: Monitoring the changes in properties of lubricant oil with different contaminants (e.g., soot particles, water, etc.) could be a reliable technique to investigate the faults that arise due to oil contamination aiding to machine maintenance. Photoacoustic sensing system has shown promises to measure such changes, however, the attempts are limited to the collection of a large number of samples for initial calibration and standardization of the process. A digital twin substituting the system may resolve these problems. In the current work, a digital twin for the photoacoustic measurements from lubricant oil has been developed through the process of: 1) designing a simulator, 2) carrying out experiments and 3) training a domain adaptation algorithm using the simulated data and testing with experimental datasets. Analysis has shown an increase in accuracy of approximately 7% for adaptation compared to the no adaptation scenario, and has established a digital twin platform for machine health analysis.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Glass micromachining using selective copper electroplating
abstract: The wet etching technique for glass micromachining is widely used in MEMS (Microelectromechanical System) to create complex structures and features at the micro-scale. One critical aspect of the glass etching process is the application of effective masking layers, which protect specific areas from the etching process. Thispaper discusses the combination of Chromium, Gold, and selective electroplated Copper layers to improve the efficiency of the masking layer. The electroplated copper layer provides a uniform and well-defined masking surface, allowing for more accurate pattern transfer onto the glass substrate. Additionally, it is a cost-effective solution, making it an attractive option for various applications. A low concentration of Hydrofluoric acid was used as the glass etchant to minimize undercutting and to enhance the control over the etching process. The etched glass substrate was characterized using an optical microscope and a confocal microscope to determine the etch depth and to analyze the surface morphology.

articleTitle: Accuracy Improved Muscle Onset and Termination Detection in EMG Signal Processing Using STKEO
abstract: In electromyogram (EMG) analysis, accurate detection of onset of the muscle activity is crucial for various applications such as prostheses, robotics, disease diagnosis, and sports science. Therefore, an automated method that can accurately detect the beginning of muscle activity while reducing the noise is highly desirable. Teager-Kaiser Energy Operator (TKEO) is commonly used to achieve this objective which comes with a few drawbacks. Therefore, in this work, we propose the use of Shannon Teager Kaiser Energy Operator (STKEO) along with a new threshold value which is calculated considering the entire EMG signal rather than the signal baseline. The threshold values are formulated in such a way that they are independent of the preset value ‘h’, as the ‘h’ value varies among literature. The results suggest that STKEO with the new threshold value performs better than TKEO and other conventional processing methods, such as rectified EMG and linear envelope, in muscle-onset detection. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated in terms of error values by considering the statistical features of the processed EMG signals. From the results, it is observed that STKEO with the modified threshold resulted in a mean error percentage of 4.75 % while the error percentage of the TKEO method resulted in an error percentage of 14.77 %.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of a High Sensitivity MEMS Tuning Fork Gyroscope
abstract: MEMS Gyros are the emerging technology for sensing angular motion of the platform they are installed on. The biggest advantages they offer is their low size, weight, cost and power consumption. In this paper we present a mode matched MEMS Tuning Fork Gyro (TFG) which offers high sensitivity and resolution. The frequency separation between drive and sense modes is only 14Hz. The TFG displays a sensitivity of 924pm/dps and a resolution of 0.001 dps. This MEMS TFG offers high sensitivity, resolution and immunity from external vibrations, which makes it a suitable choice for any device that needs to measure and control angular motion in industrial, medical, automotive, aerospace or defence sector applications.

articleTitle: Textronic e-skins or bioadaptive second skins for Infant sleep environments
abstract: Sleep is essential for all human beings including infants. Infant sleep environment should provide adequate support to the sleeping infants and mitigate the risks associated with the infant’s growth and wellbeing. Infant sleep environments comprising of Textronic e-skins or bioadaptive second skins with sensing and actuating capabilities can alleviate the risks of SIDS (sudden infant death syndrome) and Atopic dermatitis in infants during sleep to a great extent. This paper discusses the sensing mechanisms of tactile e-skins and the advantages of using textile substrates in tactile e-skins. Additionally, the need for incorporating tactile e-skins in infant sleep environments and the functionalization of textiles as tactile e-skins is highlighted. Furthermore, the paper briefly explains the design, and transduction principles of modified textile e-skins.

articleTitle: AMaizeD: An End to End Pipeline for Automatic Maize Disease Detection
abstract: This research paper presents AMaizeD: An End to End Pipeline for Automatic Maize Disease Detection, an automated framework for early detection of diseases in maize crops using multispectral imagery obtained from drones. We also develop a custom hand-collected dataset focusing specifically on maize crops was meticulously gathered by expert researchers and agronomists. The dataset encompasses a diverse range of maize varieties, cultivation practices, and environmental conditions, capturing various stages of maize growth and disease progression. By leveraging multispectral imagery, the framework benefits from improved spectral resolution and increased sensitivity to subtle changes in plant health. The proposed framework employs a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as feature extractors and segmentation techniques to identify both the maize plants and their associated diseases. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in detecting a range of maize diseases, including common rust, grey leaf spot and leaf blight. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the custom hand-collected dataset and contributes to the field of automated disease detection in agriculture, offering a practical solution for early identification of diseases in maize crops using advanced machine learning techniques and deep learning architectures.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Flexible Device for Real-Time Enzyme Free Uric Acid Detection
abstract: Uric Acid, an end product of purine metabolism, is a crucial biomolecule in biological fluids like blood serum and is directly associated with various cardiovascular and renal diseases. This work demonstrates the detection and quantification of uric acid using a screen-printed electrode modified with carboxylic acid functionalized multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT-COOH/SPE). Here, the screen-printed electrodes are fabricated over flexible OHP sheets with a microfluidic reservoir. Surface morphological analysis of MWCNT-COOH/SPE is done through microscopic characterization. Differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) and Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) techniques are used for the electrochemical characterization of the device. The device is tested for a linear range of uric acid from 10 μM to 1000 μM and the limit of detection (LoD) and limit of quantification (LoQ) obtained are 4.29 μM and 14.31 μM, respectively. Further, the real sample analysis using blood serum substantiated the applicability and feasibility of the sensor. This device demonstrated a sensitive, enzyme-less sensing of uric acid with a potential to be used in bedside analysis.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fusion Bonding of Fused Silica through Surface Treatments: A Comparative Study
abstract: Wafer bonding is a process in Micro Electro Mechanical Systems (MEMS) and microelectronics fabrication, allowing for integrating different materials and devices into a unified structure. Fusion bonding, a specific type of wafer bonding, offers several advantages, including high bonding strength, excellent thermal stability, and compatibility with various materials. This technique directly joins two substrates without requiring intermediate layers, making it a preferred choice in many applications. In the proposed work, a comparison study of the various surface activation techniques on different glass samples to modify the surface properties for better bonding strength with low bonding temperatures. The surface-activated samples are characterized using Raman Spectroscopy to identify the best suitable treatment for fusion bonding. Further, fused silica - fused silica samples are directly bonded at 400 °C temperature after surface activation. The bond strength of these bonded glass samples is measured using Die shear tester.

articleTitle: Stable, in-situ Developed Silver-Laser Induced Graphene (Ag-LIG) composite for SERS-based Uric Acid Detection
abstract: This study presents a method for easy and direct detection of uric acid using Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) by in-situ synthesized Ag-LIG. Herein, Ag was uniformly distributed all over the Laser-Induced Graphene (LIG) matrix. This enhances the electromagnetic field leading to the production of the enhanced Raman spectra. Various characterization techniques were employed to observe crystalline, morphological, and lattice vibrations. The C-N stretching, and C-H bending were observed corresponding to varying concentrations. This confirms the detection of uric acid on the surface of Ag-LIG.
