The as-prepared electrode exhibited a detection limit of approximately 60 µM for uric acid, manifesting the simple and direct detection of uric acid.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Differential Resonant Pressure Sensor
abstract: Pressure is one of the critical physical attributes that need to be continuously monitored, accurately measured, and recorded in most of manufacturing industries. This paper proposed a novel depiction of a differential resonant-based pressure sensor with a circular diaphragm and boss structure for gauging pressure in the range of 0–10 bar. The applied pressure is converted into a differential frequency signal at the two beams having one edge rigidly fixed and the other one, connected to a central structure which is coupled to the boss structure of the diaphragm. Both the analytical and numerical modeling were performed on the sensor design. Optimum sensor dimensions were scaled during numerical simulation in such a way that the diaphragm bestows maximum deflection when pressure is applied to it. The differential arrangement of the beams also helps in maintaining their stability for any ambient temperature divergence. Analytical model results performed using MATLAB were also found to be in accordance with the numerical simulation done on COMSOL Multiphysics. Stainless steel was used as the material for the simulations and was also intended to be the material for the fabrication of the sensor. Using stainless steel as the fabricating material and the sensor’s self-packaging design gives it the ability to perform well even at high temperatures and also provides protection from general corrosive environments

articleTitle: A Label-Free Low-Cost Radio Frequency Driven Noninvasive Lab-on-Chip System for Creatinine Detection
abstract: This paper illustrates a label-free, low-cost, fast detection of creatinine using a noninvasive lab-on-a-chip (LoC) Interdigitated capacitor (IDC) based sensor. Creatinine is a metabolic product of creatine phosphate in muscles, which provides energy to muscle tissues. The detection is done on an IDC made of copper (Cu) metal over an FR4 substrate. The sensor has been designed using a high-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) tool. Then the design is fabricated over the FR4 printed circuit board (PCB) and tested using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). The creatinine sample under the test is confined using a Polylactic Acid (PLA) wall attached to the sensor. A 52 MHz difference is observed between the simulated and experimental operating frequencies. The principal idea implemented in the biosensor design is to track the shift in the operating frequency in the presence of different concentrations of creatinine diluted in water and compare it with the operating frequency of the sensor with water as a reference. The testing is done in the medical range of 0.5 mg/dL to 2 mg/dL of creatinine solution.

articleTitle: High Precision Sensor Probe for Beam-Tilt Alignment Based on a Quadrant Photodetector
abstract: This paper describes the development of a laser beam positioning sensor based on a quadrant photodetector. The sensor was a critical component of a wider alignment system. It was developed to meet the stringent 45 μrad precision requirement for the orientation of the optical interferometry cavity for the length measurement in the new calculable cross-capacitor at the National Measurement Institute, Australia. This system has been used to align the optical cavity to the capacitor’s axis to within 110 μrad, which is corrected for, with an uncertainty of 6 μrad, well within the required precision.

articleTitle: Canonical Applications of Stereo Vision and Depth Sensing
abstract: Calculating spatial relationships between objects in three dimensions is crucial for applications in the field of self-driving automobiles, robotics, computer vision, space terrain mapping and virtual reality. Advanced camera imaging technology can capture images with highest resolution in two dimensions. However, the depth or distance of an object from the camera is necessarily lost. The paper discusses implementation of a novel stereo vision method for depth perception involving use of two cameras. Accuracy, resolution and range tradeoffs for depth estimation were evaluated. Precision in depth sensing under adverse lighting conditions was improved using sophisticated image processing techniques. The proposed algorithm was integrated with a robot system and canonical applications such as acquisition of stationary target object from a group of similar objects having different sizes and located at different distances were demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable SensorNet for Industry 5.0 Applications using Arduino Due/ESP32 and Xbee S2C Based on IEEE 802.15.4 Protocol with Programmable Sensor Array
abstract: This paper presents a wireless sensing platform for Industrial applications such as Industrial 5.0. It uses Xbee S2C and Arduino Due/ESP32 for wireless communication and offers customizable data resolution, sensor array size and synchronization at the same sampling iteration. The system effectively monitors reference trajectories up to 20 Hz and eliminates costly wired connections, improving data acquisition efficiency. This study contributes to the development of wireless telemetry systems for even Industrial 5.0 implementation.

articleTitle: Development of an IoT-based portable Weather Station with parameter monitoring and notifications for precision farming
abstract: Precision Agriculture leverages technology to revolutionize modern farming. A pivotal challenge within the agricultural sector revolves around elevating productivity and quality while circumventing the need for repetitive physical inspections. The inherent unpredictability and diversity of meteorological conditions pose significant hurdles for farmers, making timely and informed decision-making a constant struggle. In this study, we introduce an exploration of IoT technology's application in field crop monitoring, aiming to enhance agricultural efficiency and productivity. Our research introduces an innovative IoT-based embedded platform, complemented by a suite of specialized sensors and an intuitive user interface. This integrated system empowers farmers to accurately track environmental conditions and their impact on crops, delivering real-time alerts through communication protocols like Lora. By enabling farmers to execute essential agricultural tasks in real-time and optimize resource utilization in alignment with crop-specific requirements, our solution promises to address the capricious nature of Indian weather conditions. Our proposed weather system represents a modest yet pivotal stride toward establishing a Precision Agriculture framework, laying the foundation for a more resilient and efficient agricultural sector.

articleTitle: Improved Driver Safety through Portable Assistive Device by Monitoring Vehicle Cabin Air Quality
abstract: In recent times, the surge in air pollution has emerged as a significant source of health problems for the general population, with a particular emphasis on drivers who face a heightened risk due to their constant exposure to harmful airborne substances while on the road. To address this issue, an innovative vehicle cabin air quality monitoring system has been designed, employing advanced CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and PM2.5 sensors to provide continuous, real-time monitoring of these critical parameters. This continuous surveillance not only enhances driver safety but also serves as a proactive measure for accident prevention. What sets this system apart is its ability to establish a predefined threshold value for initiating notifications, enabling timely actions such as ventilation or activation of air purification systems. This feature is a novel approach to prevent driver fatigue, drowsiness, and protracted exposure to harmful gases, thereby mitigating the potential long-term health consequences. An important point of distinction is that CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentrations exceeding 1000 ppm can lead to driver fatigue and sleepiness. Furthermore, this cutting-edge device monitors not only CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and PM2.5 but also temperature and humidity in real-time, utilizing this data to calculate an Air Quality Index (AQI). The device then generates tailored notifications for the driver, serving as a comprehensive safeguard mechanism to preempt any adverse events for both the driver and the passengers inside the vehicle.

articleTitle: Sensory Maze: A camera-based remote expression therapy interface
abstract: In typical social settings, it can be difficult for autistic people, especially children, to express their feelings or recognize facial expressions. Even though modern communication technologies have made progress in making basic communication easier, they frequently lack the range of expression that is required for effective emotional communication. Emotion Expression Recognition (EER) is an arising field that means to peruse and decipher the feelings communicated by people continuously. In this paper, we present a user interface called Sensory Maze, that aims to teach how to express emotions, or how to identify emotions made by other people. Sensory Maze is a game that consolidates EER as a fundamental part, permitting users to obtain emotion/expression therapy in their home setting. Sensory Maze relies on a webcam that captures the facial images in real-time and uses faceapi.js to run facial expression classification models on the browser to give real-time feedback. The system has three distinct levels, starting from a virtual therapy session where the subjects are given feedback on the expression they are asked to make, to a level where a situation is presented to them, and the system verifies if they are reacting with the correct emotion. We also present a study of the performance of the system with respect to parameters such as illumination condition, presence of other subjects in the scene, and eyeglasses worn by the subject.

articleTitle: Functionalized Carbon Cloth Device for pH Sensing
abstract: The assessment of pH is of significant importance in evaluating water quality, as it has huge implications for taste perception, chemical reactions, and biological processes. This work demonstrates a simple and promising method of a potentiometric device for pH sensing with a response time of less than 1 minute. This device is developed by electropolymerizing aniline (PANI), a conducting polymer on the surface of carbon cloth (CC). CC is utilized as a working electrode and sealed with a customized acrylic design to form a 3-electrode system. The morphological study is conducted to understand the formation of emeraldine salt form of PANI. A wide pH range of 2 to 12 is tested by using open circuit voltammetry and the sensitivity of the proposed senor is found to be 1.79 mV pH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. Moreover, the interference analysis is performed utilizing alkaline metals and weak acids. Subsequently, real samples analysis was carried out, by using commercially available lake water samples, observing a maximum error of 10.85%. The device showed a wide range, good sensitivity and applicability in real time pH monitoring.

articleTitle: Novel Method of Hermetic Sealing of Electronics Package by Electron Beam Welding
abstract: This paper describes a process which is used to hermetically seal electronics packages using a welding technique called electron beam welding (EBW). The E-Beam welding is done between dissimilar materials of packaging without using any filler material. In this type of welding, components are welded to melt and fuse together, leading to a permanent joint between the Cover (cap) and Header of an electronics package. The seal is achieved without causing much thermal damage to the package. There are many ways to seal an electronics package, but electron beam welding is one of the methods which is used to hermetically seal electronics packages. Consequently, this is an attempt to hermetically seal an electronics package (TO package) utilizing EBW.The importance given to quality of seal is because the end product has a wide application range from aerospace to marine. Improper sealing of packaging devices to get exposed to moisture, harmful gases and impurities which may damage the device in long run. Hence, mechanical characterization like the helium leak test is carried out to confirm the quality of the weld or seal.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain for Future Cyber Threat Intelligence
abstract: Considering the rapid integration of smart technologies into our daily lives, the risk of cyber-attacks has increased and mitigating such risks in smart systems requires practical approaches. Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) has been considered a powerful technique for developing successful and mature proactive tools for cyber threat detection and mitigation. However, with evolving threat landscape, it has been crucial to develop and implement comprehensive, robust CTI solutions to ensure the security and resilience of interconnected smart systems. Recently, the two emerging technologies of artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain have gained significant attention in the field of cybersecurity. AI and blockchain offer novel ways to improve security, privacy, and efficiency in different areas of cyber security. However, a lack of research on the integration of AI and blockchain in CTI is considered. In this paper, we propose the integration of AI and blockchain in CTI and assess their advantages and disadvantages to explore how AI and blockchain can enhance CTI. We also discuss the role of AI and blockchain across various phases of a CTI life cycle in a detailed manner.

articleTitle: An Enhanced VGG16-based CNN for Classification of Cyanobacteria
abstract: Water bodies play a vital role in the survival of living organisms in many ways. However, the major problem with these natural water bodies is the formation of harmful algal blooms (HABs). HABs contain toxins meant for humans, animals, and marine ecosystems and block sunlight and oxygen from reaching them. There should be proper monitoring against these algal blooms. Manual detection of HABs through in-situ sampling is accurate but it is both time-consuming and difficult to perform. One of the major types of these HABs is cyanobacteria. This study proposes a novel approach utilizing an enhanced version of the VGG16 architecture implemented in a convolutional neural network (CNN) model. This innovative model harnesses the power of deep learning to efficiently and accurately identify cyanobacteria from microscopic images. The model leverages architectural enhancements and transfer learning techniques to extract intricate cyanobacterial features, yielding precise classifications. By training on a diverse dataset of cyanobacteria species, the model demonstrates a remarkable classification accuracy of 89.6% on the test set. The automated and reliable cyanobacteria classification provided by the enhanced VGG16-based CNN empowers informed decision-making and proactive management of water resources affected by HABs. As a vital tool in environmental monitoring, this model advances our capability to address the pressing challenges posed by cyanobacterial blooms.

articleTitle: Microwave based Non-Invasive Localized Anomaly Detection in Wood as a Biological Tissue Phantom
abstract: Localized anomalies in biological tissues, such as tumors, wounds, and edema, possess microwave properties starkly different from the healthy tissues. Microwave imaging (MWI) utilizes the changes in the electric properties of the tissues to detect anomalies in these tissues by forming an image of the test region. We present a novel, non-invasive technique to detect the localized anomalies in biological tissues using microwaves for in-vivo applications. Here, the scattering measurements of the test specimen are carried out in the microwave frequency range using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA), and a modified calibration technique is utilized for de-embedding the calibration plane to the surface of the sample. Wood is used as a biological tissue phantom in the present situation, where a localized anomaly is introduced. The transmission characteristics of the wood sample measured using the VNA are utilized to estimate the change in attenuation and phase constant due to the introduction of an anomaly in the specimen. These changes are subsequently used to compute the dielectric constant (ϵ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) and loss tangent (tan δ) of the test specimen. The results suggest that the proposed technique can efficiently differentiate between healthy tissues and tissues with anomalies, with a variation of nearly 50 % in the complex permittivity between the two.

articleTitle: Sensors Enabling Precision Spraying in Agriculture: A Case Study
abstract: Precision Agriculture is the use of emerging technologies to increase crop yields and profitability while reducing the levels of inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, herbicides, pesticide, water required for cultivation. It aims to minimize the input, labor costs as well as environmental effects. Spraying is one of the important activities in crop production and includes the application of fertilizers, herbicides, pesticides, and fungicides. Traditionally these chemicals are broadcast over the entire field at uniform rates. But Precision agriculture encourages or proposes the spraying of chemicals only at the right place, in the right quantity. This may include application of herbicide only on the weed, application of pesticide only on the pests and application of fertilizer at variable rates as per the needs of the crop/soil. Sensors have been key elements in enabling such type of spraying. This paper discusses a review of the important and most significant sensors for precision spraying using self-propelled or trailed agricultural sprayers. It covers 3 areas of precision spraying: selective spraying, boom stability and height control and positioning systems, where sensors are playing a significant role. The different types of sensors in each area and their advantages, disadvantages and future scope are covered.

articleTitle: Aerodynamics and Sensing Analysis for Efficient Drone-Based Parcel Delivery
abstract: In an era of rapid urbanization and e-commerce growth, efficient parcel delivery methods are crucial. This paper presents a detailed study of the aerodynamics and sensing analysis of drones for parcel delivery. Utilizing Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), the study offers a comprehensive airflow analysis, revealing the aerodynamic forces affecting drone stability due to payload capacity. A multidisciplinary approach is employed, integrating mechanical design, control theory, and sensing systems to address the complex issue of parcel positioning. The experimental validation section rigorously tests different size payloads and their positions and impact on drones with maximum thrusts of 2000 gf. The findings prove the drone’s capacity to lift a large payload that covers up to 50 percent of the propeller, thereby contributing to optimizing drone designs and sustainable parcel delivery systems. It has been observed that the drone can lift a large payload smoothly when placed above the drone, with an error rate as low as 0.1 percent for roll, pitch, and yaw. This work paved the way for more versatile, real-world applications of drone technology, setting a new standard in the field.

articleTitle: Cyber Security Resilience in Industrial Control Systems using Defence-in-Depth and Zero Trust
abstract: An Industrial Control System (ICS) can be seen as a comprehensive class of automation systems employed to provide control and monitoring functionalities in manufacturing and industrial sectors. There has been a trend to include critical infrastructure across ICS sectors for safe and efficient operations. However, integrating critical infrastructure with public networks has exposed ICSs to cyber-attacks. As traditional ICSs have not been designed to handle security threats, existing vulnerabilities should be identified, and proper methods must be developed to make systems cyber-resilient. In this paper, we discuss the challenges of cyber security resilience in ICS networks. We provide the functionalities of an ICS architecture and vulnerabilities in an ICS network. Significantly, we discuss defence-in-depth for ICS networks based on prevention, detection, and incident response, and the incorporation of zero trust principles. Finally, we outline potential future activities to address those challenges.

articleTitle: Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Indoor UAV Navigation in Confined Spaces
abstract: In this paper, we address the challenge of navigating through unknown indoor environments using autonomous aerial robots within confined spaces. The core of our system involves the integration of key sensor technologies, including depth sensing from the ZED 2i camera, IMU data, and LiDAR measurements, facilitated by the Robot Operating System (ROS) and RTAB-Map. Through custom designed experiments, we demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of this approach. Our results showcase a promising navigation accuracy, with errors as low as 0.4 meters, and mapping quality characterized by a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of just 0.13 m. Notably, this performance is achieved while maintaining energy efficiency and balanced resource allocation, addressing a crucial concern in UAV applications. Flight tests further underscore the precision of our system in maintaining desired flight orientations, with a remarkable error rate of only 0.1%. This work represents a significant stride in the development of autonomous indoor UAV navigation systems, with potential applications in search and rescue, facility inspection, and environmental monitoring within GPS-denied indoor environments.

articleTitle: Prognostic System for Power-Electronic IGBT Modules in Electric, Hybrid Electric and Fuel-Cell Vehicles Using Machine Learning
abstract: Power electronic modules in electric vehicles are in charge of converting and managing the electric power supply of the system. In this project, a predictive warning system that monitors the voltage at the insulated gate of the bipolar transistor was designed. The method is hardware-based and MATLAB/Simulink-verified. Due to unavoidable power loss from heat generation and fluctuating inverter phase currents, power modules are subject to thermomechanical stress and wear. Increased forward on-voltage, leakage current, thermal impedance, small-signal impedance, and noise level are some early indications of failure. Wire-bond lift-off and cracks at silicon-substrate or substrate-baseplate solder junctions are the leading causes of the failure mechanisms. An IGBT-based full bridge inverter was designed for hardware implementation. Simulink was used to map the progressive decline and a few little signals. The power cycling test was performed to examine and track the performance of the power modules with the aid of an algorithm to stress test the module. The junction temperature was calculated using relevant details about VCESat’s temperature estimate. The solder junctions deteriorated throughout this process, which raised the overall heat resistance of the module before the wire-bond lift-off failure. The module’s temperature rose, and the on-voltage dropped. After the failure, the IGBT module on-voltage exhibited a sizable increase. A prognostic subroutine took approximately a hundredth of a second and had no impact on performance to observe the irregular variation of the VCESat under particular current and temperature circumstances. If there was a 15% or more significant disparity between the measured and reference values of VCESat, the system issued a warning signal. Using the signature deterioration trace on VCESat, an IGBT module prognostic system was created without significantly increasing the cost of the existing vehicle-drive system. Lastly, the system was implemented using a Machine Learning algorithm, K Nearest Neighbors (KNN).

articleTitle: Characterization of Tool Eccentricity of a CNC Milling Machine Using High Speed Imaging
abstract: Tool eccentricity is a common phenomenon in the milling process and has a significant impact on machining precision and surface quality. This paper presents a cost-effective eccentricity measuring system using high-speed imaging technique for a CNC end mill in its dynamic conditions. Traditional methods such as capacitance and eddy current sensing techniques, require close placement of the sensing probe to tool, whereas high-speed imaging offers a relatively remote, easy to calibrate and affordable solution. Capture of sharp and high-resolution video or image sequence of a high- speed rotating tool enables us to accurately measure its eccentricity. We present a system configured for 37 μm resolution and a test case of eccentricity measurement of 366 μm at the tip and 293 μm at the center of the tool while it is rotating at 6000 rpm. The novelty of this system lies in the utilization of high-speed synchronous strobing of illumination, allowing it to work seamlessly with various commercial compact cameras that do not offer access to their shutter trigger electronically.

articleTitle: An Interfacing Scheme with Improved Bandwidth for Multi-Current-Output Sensors
abstract: The paper presents a simple interfacing electronics suitable for a sensor system, involving multiple current-output sensors. The proposed interface selects and processes the individual sensor nodes, and then efficiently estimates the sensor-current and/or their combination. The novel design of the interface, which comprises an improved current-sense circuit, a switching logic and multi-regiming signal conditioner, renders many meritorious features. The salient features include improved bandwidth, reduced effects of ADC resolution, as well as the ability to provide customized design as per user requirements. The methodology and performance evaluation of this interfacing scheme is described in the paper. The test results, using simulation as well as hardware-based tests on a four-sensor system, demonstrate the performance of the scheme. The maximum non-linearity for a range of (10 nA, 160 nA) is obtained as 0.184%. The improvement in bandwidth is about 9.9 kHz (factor of improvement = 100). The working of gain regimes is shown adequately for single as well as multiple current output sensing. This technique is useful for various instruments such as magnetic field sensors and photodiodes.

articleTitle: Early Detection Framework for Gait Disorders Using an IoT LiDAR-Based Monitoring System in Outdoor Spaces
abstract: In the pursuit of advancing healthcare technologies and promoting the well-being of the elderly population, this paper presents a conceptual framework for early detection of gait disorders through public IoT-based health monitoring. As global life expectancy continues to rise, there is an increasing need for unobtrusive health monitoring systems that can facilitate the early identification of health issues, particularly among the elderly. While many healthcare monitoring technologies exist, their limited accessibility and deployment in controlled environments or healthcare facilities present challenges. To address this, our innovative concept proposes a smart IoT-based outdoor health monitoring system, specifically designed for public spaces such as parks and supermarkets. This system aims to collect data on mobility, posture, and gait, recognising the crucial role that gait plays in an individual's well-being. The proposed system leverages the power of the Internet of Things (IoT) to gather data seamlessly from individuals in their everyday environments, creating a more holistic and real-world understanding of their health. By analysing gait patterns and deviations, our conceptual framework aims to serve as an early warning system for health-care providers, caregivers, and individuals themselves, alerting them to potential health concerns and enabling proactive intervention. This concept, while in its early stages, holds immense promise for addressing the challenges of an ageing population and reducing healthcare disparities. It aligns with the broader vision of harnessing emerging technologies to enhance the quality of life for the elderly.

articleTitle: Smart City Air Quality Monitoring supported IoT ecosystem
abstract: Outdoor air pollution is a serious worldwide problem, affecting millions of people, with serious consequences for public health, economy and for social issues. Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a response to the creation of intelligent monitoring systems that can be used for management and identification of pollution sources, and for health protection. With the development of new devices and technologies that allow the creation of real-time monitoring applications, this reality has become increasingly relevant nowadays. This paper aims to introduce an implementation of an IoT system for outdoor air quality monitoring, based on multichannel smart sensing system with LoRa communication capability. The system incorporates low cost and low consumption sensors capable of detecting different air pollutants, as well as temperature and humidity. To achieve a long-distance transmission of readings with low energy consumption, the use of LoRa technology was adopted due to its characteristics. The periodicity of sending readings to the network is based on the level of urban traffic in a certain location. Furthermore, a web application is presented, which allows the user to monitor in real time and to carry out a temporal analysis of the measurements taken by the system.

articleTitle: Resistance Network Synthesis for Analog Thermistor-Linearizer Circuits using Differential Evolution and Graph Laplacian
abstract: Thermistors are widely deployed for measuring temperature in various industrial applications. A thermistor is a compact, accurate temperature sensor with high sensitivity and excellent operating range. The transfer characteristic of the thermistor is a non-linear function. This paper proposes an evolutionary algorithm based approach for synthesizing resistive networks for analog linearizer circuits with minimum non-linearity and at least a minimum sensitivity value. The approach uses concepts of resistance distance and graph Laplacian matrix to formulate an optimization problem. The equivalent resistances of synthesized resistive networks are transformed into voltages using simple opamp-based circuits. It is shown that the proper choice of circuit parameters enhances the performance of the designed linearization circuits. The parameters of the linearization circuits are computed using a differential evolution algorithm. We propose and compare multiple circuit topologies; the best of which achieves a non-linearity of 0.4%, with a commercial thermistor, in the range of [0, 120]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup>C with a sensitivity of 2.8 mV/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup>C.

articleTitle: Enhancing Disaster Mitigation: Mobile-GIS Sister Village Evacuation Route System for Mount Merapi Eruption in Yogyakarta
abstract: The Mobile-GIS Sister Village Evacuation Route (MSVER) system was devised and implemented in order to enhance Yogyakarta’s Mount Merapi eruption mitigation and evacuation. The 2010 eruption of Mount Merapi, with its pyroclastic flows and volcanic ashfall, posed a threat to local residents. In response, the Center for Volcanology and Geological Disaster Mitigation (PVMBG) issued evacuation orders with variable safe zone radii, necessitating meticulous route planning and communication. This study suggests MSVER, which utilizes GIS and Sister Villages to address these problems. Using GIS on mobile devices, the system provides real-time data on disaster-prone areas, evacuation routes, meeting points, and disaster-resistant villages. The BPPTKG provides status updates for Mount Merapi. MSVER system development involves establishing optimization criteria for evacuation routes, such as distance, speed, density, and obstacles. The Merapi Evacuation Route app helps users locate danger zones, discover evacuation routes and gathering sites, and comprehend Mount Merapi’s eruption status and risks. It also contains information on the population and disaster-resilient villages. In conclusion, the MSVER system employs GIS and Sister Villages to assist communities in Yogyakarta in preparing for and responding to Mount Merapi eruptions. This ingenious strategy saves lives and serves as an example of how to use indigenous knowledge and technology to combat natural disasters.

articleTitle: Water Quality Index Prediction System Using IoT Enabled Sensor Suite and Machine Learning
abstract: There is an increase in the necessity to monitor the water quality of different water resources as nowadays, clean drinking water is not in abundance and water quality needs to be known beforehand to prevent the occurrence of diseases associated with consuming unfit water. This paper presents an approach to determining the water quality index (WQI) of a water sample by measuring the essential water quality parameters such as pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), electrical conductivity (EC), total dissolved solids (TDS), turbidity, and temperature. For calculating and predicting the WQI, the Canadian water quality index (CWQI) calculation is used in this work. An IoT and cloud-based solution module that can be used to access the acquired sensor data and make preliminary conclusions as well as the quality of water is developed and presented. Furthermore, machine learning is used to predict the WQI of the samples. Conclusive results on water quality are decided based on the safe ranges outlined by the World Health Organization (WHO) and CPCB that outline the range for safe water. The training validation and prediction results of the machine learning models such as long short-term memory models (LSTMs) and neural networks are presented and the CWQI calculated for the water samples collected and tested are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation Combined With Listening to Indian Classical Raga on Situation Awareness
abstract: Both listening to music and using transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) have been proposed as methods to enhance cognitive performance on a temporary basis. To date, there has been no research conducted on the potential cognitive performance benefits that could arise from the combination of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) and listening to Indian classical raga music. In the present study, the objective was to investigate whether the combination of anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) applied to the medial prefrontal cortex (at a current intensity of 2 mA for a duration of 20 minutes) along with simultaneous listening to Indian classical raga music has the potential to enhance situation awareness compared to a sham stimulation condition without music. A randomized sham-controlled crossover study involved 26 healthy adults aged 18 to 24 years who participated in two different neurostimulation conditions: one involving transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with music listening (tDCS+Music), and the other involving a sham-tDCS condition. The level of situation awareness was evaluated before and after the stimulation sessions using a Situation Awareness Global Assessment Technique (SAGAT). The results of the SAGAT assessment demonstrated an improvement in performance in the tDCS+Raga condition. The findings from the study suggest that combining the use of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) with listening to Raga music enhances situation awareness. These results highlight the potential value of incorporating neurostimulation techniques alongside Raga music to improve situation awareness.

articleTitle: A Simple, Linear Circuit for Measuring fF Range of Capacitances with Improved Performance
abstract: Capacitive sensing is a common approach used in many measurement applications. Sometimes, the change in the magnitude of the capacitive sensor can be only femto-Farads. As the circuitry that can detect such small capacitance changes can be extremely expensive and complicated, the authors in one of their earlier publications, presented a simple circuit that detects such minute changes with good sensitivity and produce the corresponding outputs linearly. The reason behind these advantages was its working principle where-in, it first performs a differencing operation followed by a differential measurement during the sensing. However, this circuit had an issue of large offset voltage which reduced its resolution. So, a negative feedback loop is now added to it to improve this feature. The subsequent performance analysis of this modified circuit is presented in this paper. The experimental results show that while all the positive features are retained, the precision and resolution improved considerably. Due to this improved performance, the scope of using this circuit for various minute capacitance measurement applications is bound to increase, for e.g. quality check of transformer oil by estimating minute traces of dissolved moisture in it.

articleTitle: SEG – Smart Exosuit Glove for Data Driven Physiotherapy
abstract: Physiotherapy and rehabilitation of the human hand play a crucial role in restoring the function and mobility of the hand movement after serious injuries or conditions affecting it. This research aims to develop an exosuit for hands, comprising a Data Glove and E-skin and software for data analysis and prediction, to observe and assess the effects and improvements in hand function among patients undergoing physiotherapy or rehabilitation for hand-related conditions. Through a comprehensive evaluation process, patients’ hand functions are assessed before, during, and after the physiotherapy sessions. The exosuit facilitates the collection of quantitative and qualitative data, allowing for a detailed analysis of progress and improvement. These measurements include range of motion, grip strength, fine motor skills, dexterity, and sensory feedback. The collected data is analyzed using advanced machine learning algorithms and statistical methods to identify trends, patterns, and correlations that can help optimize the rehabilitation process and personalize treatment plans for each patient. This integration offers several advantages, such as enhanced accuracy, increased sensitivity, and improved flexibility compared to traditional assessment methods. This research aims to contribute to the development of more effective and personalized physiotherapy and rehabilitation approaches by leveraging the potential of emerging technologies.

articleTitle: Waste Detection and Classification Using Yolo Algorithm and Sensors
abstract: Improper waste management poses health risks and environmental problems. In India, municipal solid waste of over 150,000 tonnes is generated on a day-to-day basis, while metro cities like Mumbai are densely polluted. Unfortunately, only a tiny fraction of the garbage is appropriately collected and handled. India is expected to produce 377,000 tonnes of trash per day by 2025. The need for effective waste segregation is highlighted by the fact that unprocessed garbage contains valuable components that can be repurposed or composted. Technologies based on deep learning provide solutions for garbage detection and classification that increase accuracy and productivity. It is possible to design robots to do jobs and lessen the exposure of humans to dangerous toxins. Utilizing sensor-based approaches, such as metal and moisture sensors, can improve waste management procedures even more. We can enhance waste management and produce a cleaner, safer environment by tackling these issues and properly utilizing innovative technologies.

articleTitle: Biosensors: Pioneering Progress in Sensing Technologies across Generations
abstract: The article explores the pivotal role of sensing materials and technologies in advancing sensor efficiency for electronic appliances. Focusing on biosensors, it delves into their evolution across three generations, highlighting their impact on environmental risk detection and disease diagnosis. The components of a typical biosensor are detailed, emphasizing the importance of key performance characteristics. The historical timeline traces significant milestones in biosensor development, from Leland Clark Jr.'s groundbreaking work to recent innovations like epidermal microfluidic sensors. The the ongoing growth and future potential of biosensors across diverse scientific and engineering domains are enormous.
